question: What is non-signaling tester, and which product-related measurement decisions depend on understanding it?
answer: In the Vault, "non-signaling" describes an RF test mode in which the tester makes parametric RF measurements on the DUT without running a full protocol/signaling connection — RX/PER/BER work is done instead via loopback or direct-test-mode style paths (e.g. R&S CMP-KM365 for WLAN nonsignaling PER, CMP-KM310 for Bluetooth nonsignaling DTM RX, and loop-based receiver quality testing with the downlink generator). A "non-signaling tester" is therefore a radio communication tester optimized for that mode: the Vault positions R&S CMP180 as the production-phase non-signaling RF measurement tester, and CMP200 together with the CMPHEAD30/CMPHEAD50 remote radio heads as the 5G NR FR2 (mmWave) nonsignaling one-box test solution for R&D and high-volume manufacturing RF parametric testing. The stated reason for non-signaling mode in production is test time: in the WLAN device production phase all RF measurements are run non-signaling to save time. Product-related measurement decisions that depend on this distinction include: (1) choosing a signaling platform (CMX500 / CMW500) versus a non-signaling production/ATE platform (CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100 K06) for a given test stage in the 5G device testing value chain, where "Non-signaling RF" is listed as its own test type; (2) qualification questions in competitive positioning — whether non-signaling ATE, multi-port production test, or factory-line non-signaling capability is required; (3) FR2 setup architecture on CMP200 (radiated mmWave vs mixed radiated/conducted IF, RRH used to shorten mmWave cabling for link budget); and (4) option/licence selection — non-signaling RX/PER options on CMP180, and on CMX500 the GPRF generator / IQ recorder / standalone TX measurement non-signaling use cases where the generator slide claims "No License required" but technology-specific ARB waveform replay needs the KWxxx licences. The Vault has no dedicated concept page defining the term itself; the usage above is what the product and solution pages support.
missing: The Vault has no dedicated concept/glossary page for "non-signaling tester" or "Non-signaling RF" (those wikilinks are unresolved stubs), so there is no single authoritative definition of the term, no explicit statement of how non-signaling differs from signaling at the protocol-stack level, and no quantified test-time or throughput comparison between signaling and non-signaling production test. The R&S CMP180 and R&S CMW100 K06 entity pages are also not shown to contain their own non-signaling positioning statements.
